name: Anastrozole
owner: generic (many); Arimidex brand held by AstraZeneca and others regionally

discovery.note: A triazole designed to reversibly bind the haem of aromatase with high selectivity.

tagline: Triazole aromatase inhibitor for hormone-receptor-positive breast cancer after menopause
summary: Anastrozole is a non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor that blocks conversion of androgens to oestrogens and lowers circulating oestradiol in postmenopausal women by over 80%. It is used as adjuvant and metastatic therapy for hormone-receptor-positive breast cancer and for risk reduction.
mechanism: After menopause, most oestrogen is made by aromatase (CYP19A1) in adipose and other peripheral tissues from adrenal androgens.

Anastrozole's triazole nitrogen coordinates the haem iron of aromatase, competitively and reversibly blocking conversion of androstenedione to oestrone and testosterone to oestradiol. Oestrogen deprivation slows growth of ER-positive tumours. In premenopausal women it is ineffective alone, because falling oestrogen raises gonadotrophins and ovarian output.
uses: Adjuvant treatment of hormone-receptor-positive early breast cancer in postmenopausal women
First- and second-line therapy of advanced breast cancer
Risk reduction in high-risk postmenopausal women (e.g. UK)

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved as Arimidex for advanced breast cancer after tamoxifen.

history.title: ATAC
history.detail: The ATAC trial shows anastrozole reduces recurrence versus tamoxifen as adjuvant therapy; FDA approves adjuvant use.

history.title: Generics
history.detail: Generic anastrozole enters the US market.

history.title: IBIS-II
history.detail: Anastrozole halves breast cancer incidence in high-risk postmenopausal women.

history.title: NICE prevention guidance
history.detail: UK guidance supports anastrozole for chemoprevention in postmenopausal high-risk women.

facts: Aromatase inhibitor arthralgia is one of the commonest reasons for stopping adjuvant therapy early.
